propositions: Multiple bundle objects for one S3 ref cause clone hard-failure (multiple updates for ref not allowed) and push rejection (cmd_push blocks at len(bundles)>1), rendering the store unclonable and push-stalled.

Upstream git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocks on input() prompts at EOF) and discards non-chosen heads by default, losing unique ticket events from divergent bundles into an append-only store.
A single lossless 2-parent merge of all divergent bundle heads, written to S3 before deleting originals, recovers append-only semantics while keeping every event reachable (no data loss).

The doctor acquires the helper's per-ref S3 lock, re-enumerates under lock, fetches all heads, iteratively merges them via rebar's existing sync reconcile semantics (with --allow-unrelated-histories for unrelated roots), writes the merged tip as a new bundle, deletes originals, then releases the lock.

Push detection of the multi-bundle signature (multiple bundles exists on server / multiple updates for ref) invokes heal_multi_bundle exactly once before retry, guarded by healed_once to prevent thrash loops.

The doctor's local merge runs under rebar's write_lock (inner) with the helper's S3 ref-lock as outer lock; conflicts in non-derived files abort without deleting remote bundles and surface fsck-recover, preserving all parents.
